capabilities: Match note names, aliases and paths per keystroke
Search every word of every note with typo and word-form tolerance
Filter results with chips for tags, types, dates, paths and links
Restrict searches to generated or manual scopes
Rank notes by the line answering a question using an optional local model
disambiguation: Not a replacement for Obsidian's search; it hands off Obsidian-specific operators like line:, block: and /regex/ to the core search.
extras: Free and open source, no telemetry or accounts. Desktop only in practice; mobile works but is not officially supported. The optional Search by meaning downloads a ~31 MB embedding model from Hugging Face, or you can supply the two model files yourself. Index and vectors are stored in IndexedDB outside the vault. The README notes Omnisearch also reads PDFs and images, which Jet does not.
intentEvidence: Jet was timed against Obsidian's own search and quick switcher, and the most-installed search plugins
motivation: The author states search is done a hundred times a day, so a hundred small waits add up, and built Jet so there is no wait.
problem: Obsidian's built-in search and quick switcher are slow to return results and only the switcher matches names, so finding a note means waiting and often retyping.

relations.evidence: Omnisearch: 212 ms. Obsidian's own search: 96 ms, and up to 2.2 s.
Another Quick Switcher | 21 ms | 21 ms | 28 ms | none | 10 ms
Does it replace Obsidian's search? No. It sits beside it.

requires.name: Hugging Face (model download for Search by meaning)

summary: Instant search plugin that matches note names and every word as you type, with typo tolerance, filters, scopes and optional on-device semantic search.
